description_en: The Khapĩchẽ Phalcā was a small Phalcā located outside the Khapĩchẽ courtyard. However, it collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes and has not been rebuilt. GTZ/udle had previously supported its renovation in 1994. Despite its small size, the Phalcā had been an important site for locals and the community's Bhairava mask was displayed here. However, at some point the mask disappeared (date unknown: according to local information, the mask was displayed in the Phalcā before it was stolen in the night during Indrajātra) and so this tradition came to an end. Community members have said that they hope to generate funding for the building's reconstruction.
description_ne: खपिंछेँ चोकको कुनामा रहेको यो फल्चा सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पमा ध्वस्त भएपछि अहिलेसम्म बनेको छैन । सन् १९९४ मा GTZ/udle को सहयोगमा यसको पुनर्निर्माण भएको थियो । आकारमा सानो भए पनि यहाँ विभिन्न उत्सवमा भैरवको मुखाकृति प्रदर्शन गरिने हुनाले यसको विशेष सांस्कृतिक महत्त्व थियो । स्थानीयले दिएको जानकारी अनुसार पहिला कुनै वर्षको इन्द्रजात्राको अवसरमा फल्चामा राखिएको भैरवको मुखाकृति हराएको हुनाले त्यो परम्परा पनि रोकियो । स्थानीयहरू यसको पुनर्निर्माणको लागि कतैबाट पहल हुने कुरामा आशावादी छन् ।

historical_events.event_description: At the request of members of the local community, Patan Conservation and Development Programme undertook the repair of the Khapiṁchẽ Phalcā in March 1994. Damage had begun from the roof, as is common in such work, and the rafters, plankings and eaves boards were rotten due to several years of monsoons. However, some of the timber planks were reusable and so were kept. The top half of the back wall was in a very poor condition because it had been built with sun dried bricks. The plinth was in a good condition.During the repair work, the roof structure was replaced with new sal timber and planks with a water proof membrane of tarfelt. The timber beam above the columns was also replaced with sal timber. All of the original timber columns were reused. The wainscote on the back wall was provided at the request of local elders. A few of the plinth's bricks were reused and the top half of the back wall was rebuilt using traditional mud mortar and old ma-aapa.The total cost, including construction, implementation and supervision, came to Rs 64,846.00
